title: RAE: A Neural Network Dimensionality Reduction Method for Nearest Neighbors Preservation in Vector Search

problem.claim: High-dimensional embedding vectors are increasingly used in retrieval-related tasks, but dimensionality reduction methods are needed without disrupting nearest-neighbor relationships.

gap.claim: PCA and UMAP have rarely been adopted to accelerate retrieval because they are unable to preserve nearest-neighbor relationships among vectors.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a Regularized Auto-Encoder for k-nearest-neighbor-preserving dimensionality reduction.
The method uses regularization terms to constrain network parameter variation and adjust singular values to control embedding magnitude changes during reduction.
The paper provides a theoretical analysis showing that the regularization establishes an upper bound on the norm distortion rate of transformed vectors.

author_reported_evidence.claim: With modest training overhead, RAE achieves a significantly higher recall rate than existing dimensionality-reduction approaches while maintaining prompt retrieval latency.
The theoretical analysis is reported to provide supportive guarantees for k-nearest-neighbor proximity through an upper bound on norm distortion.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-dimensional embeddings are increasingly used, while existing dimensionality-reduction methods do not reliably preserve nearest-neighbor relationships for retrieval acceleration.
The authors propose a regularized auto-encoder for preserving k-nearest-neighbor relationships during dimensionality reduction.
Regularization constrains parameter variation and adjusts singular values to control embedding magnitude changes.
The regularization is analyzed as establishing an upper bound on transformed-vector norm distortion, supporting nearest-neighbor proximity.
The method is reported to improve recall over existing dimensionality-reduction approaches while maintaining prompt retrieval latency with modest training overhead.
